heroLead: Soothing, restorative 1:1 sessions of gentle movement, breathwork, and deep rest, built around your body and how you feel through changing life stages. Practised alongside the care your doctor provides.
empathyLabel: You don't have to do this alone
empathyText: Hormones shift through every life stage. Yoga can be a soothing, steadying part of your week, supporting rest and calm alongside the care your doctor provides.
helpsH2: How yoga can support hormonal health.
helpsSubhead: Four gentle levers, working together, and the first one does most of the lifting.

levers.title: Rest for real tiredness
levers.body: Broken sleep and deep tiredness come with many hormonal stages. Restorative postures and guided relaxation help you wind down and rest more deeply.

levers.title: Calmer days, steadier moods
levers.body: When stress and mood swings run high, slow breathing and meditation help you feel more settled and even from one day to the next.

levers.title: Comfort in the body
levers.body: Gentle mobility, hip- and abdomen-friendly poses, and a cooling breath, traditionally used to help you feel more comfortable through cramps, tension, and warm flushes.

levers.title: A routine you can keep
levers.body: Gentle, consistent movement supports an active routine and a healthy weight: a steady habit that carries you through changing life stages.

whoForText: Anyone moving through changing hormonal stages (monthly cycles, pregnancy recovery, perimenopause, or menopause) who wants a gentle, restorative practice to support rest, sleep, and a sense of steadiness.
testimonialQuote: Perimenopause knocked my sleep and my moods sideways. The restful, restorative pace was exactly right. I sleep better now and feel far more like myself.

faqs.q: Can yoga balance my hormones or treat PCOS, thyroid, or menopause?
faqs.a: No. Yoga supports rest, calm, and an active routine alongside the care your doctor provides. It isn't a treatment for any condition, and you shouldn't change medication without your doctor.

faqs.q: Can I practise during my period?
faqs.a: Yes, gently. Tell your teacher and we'll adapt, often leaving out strong inversions if you prefer.
Yes. Many people find the calming, restorative focus and cooling breath soothing, and we adapt to how you feel each session.

faqs.q: Could I be pregnant, and does that change things?
faqs.a: Tell your teacher and we'll switch to a pregnancy-safe approach, and ask for your doctor or midwife's clearance first.

faqs.q: How soon might I notice anything?
faqs.a: Everyone is different. Many people first notice calmer stress and better sleep, and consistency helps the most.

safetyTitle: Yoga supports your care, it doesn't replace it
safetyText: These sessions support your overall wellbeing and are practised alongside professional medical care. They are not a substitute for diagnosis, treatment, or medication. Please tell your teacher about any conditions or symptoms so they can adapt your session safely, and keep your doctor in the loop.
metaDescription: Gentle, restorative 1:1 yoga for hormonal health: soothing movement, breathwork, and deep rest that may support better sleep, steadier energy, and calmer days through changing life stages. First session free.
